item.text:
**Bottom line:** mostly positive. Biden’s 2024 record shows sustained investment in technology, workforce skills, health-cost reduction, administrative modernization, and competition policy. The clearest counterevidence is trade protectionism on China, which makes the investment/regulatory environment less open and more unpredictable.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|

That makes the productivity case plausible but partly electoral. | 5B.6, 5B.3 |

**Search gap**
- I found strong positive evidence across all six pillars, especially semiconductors, AI safety, drug-price negotiation, FAFSA modernization, and competition rules.
- The clearest negative evidence was not neglect of infrastructure or education; it was trade protectionism and some short-term political framing around student debt relief.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Biden broadly undermined infrastructure, health, or administrative capacity; the record is more “active state-building with some policy friction” than “capture or neglect.”
